name: stylus-nexus
description: Stylus Nexus plugins for Claude Code + Codex.

plugins.name: release-ops
plugins.description: Five skills for getting a release out the door. npm-publish runs the full path -- preflight checks, semver bump, changelog entry, git push, publish -- and rotates an expired npm token through the browser instead of stopping to ask for a one-time code. version-check reads the commits since the last tag and recommends the bump. pr-wait blocks on CI checks and optionally merges when they pass. dependency-upgrade treats bulk bumps as a gated pipeline rather than a single update command, running type checks, tests, and E2E between batches. the-waiting estimates how long running CI jobs have left from their own history and spots runs stuck behind a cancelled run that never stopped.

plugins.name: second-opinion
plugins.description: Five skills built on one premise: a single model's confident answer is not evidence. llm-council runs a question through five advisors who analyse independently before synthesis; plan-arbiter compares, judges, and merges competing plans rather than picking one on vibes; spec-review checks a spec's claims against the real codebase before code is written, catching wrong data-model assumptions early; agent-watchdog audits another agent's work from its session or transcript; and debug-feedback-loop builds a deterministic pass/fail signal for a bug BEFORE hypothesising about causes.

plugins.name: hardening
plugins.description: Five pre-launch security gates covering the unglamorous failures that reach production. rate-limit-audit inventories every endpoint calling a paid API and every auth endpoint, then checks each actually has a limit; exposure-scan checks installed packages across npm, Go, PyPI, RubyGems and MCP servers against threat-intelligence catalogs for known-compromised releases; auth-hardening is a session, cookie, CSRF and OAuth-scope audit; webhook-reliability covers signature verification, idempotency, retry and dead letters in both directions; and privacy-audit inventories exactly what user data is collected and where it lands, checked against the code rather than the policy.

plugins.name: reporting-comms
plugins.description: Seven skills for turning agent output into something a person actually wants to read, and getting their judgment back. html renders plans, reviews, research, and comparisons as a single self-contained HTML artifact; visual-plan and visual-recap turn text plans and git diffs into interactive documents with diagrams, file maps, and annotated code; recap-table produces before/after and what-changed tables on demand; writing-clearly-and-concisely and human-writing tighten the prose itself, stripping AI tells, corporate register, and padding; and redline runs the other direction, handing a draft back to the human to edit and comment on in a browser and returning one Markdown review the agent applies.

plugins.name: codebase-intel
plugins.description: Four skills for building an accurate picture of a codebase and the libraries it depends on, before committing to a change. codebase-health surfaces complexity hotspots, churn, and bus factor when onboarding or planning a refactor; codebase-architecture-scanner generates layered architecture documentation with C4 and sequence diagrams; grill-with-docs challenges a plan against the existing domain model and sharpens terminology; and read-the-damn-docs stops guesses about third-party API behavior by going to the current documentation first.

plugins.name: ship-pipeline
plugins.description: Eight repo-agnostic skills for the ship half of the development loop. start-issue (full-issue intake including comments, prior-art check, baseline capture, branch naming), db-truth (ground schema claims in the live database before designing against them; confirm migrations actually landed after applying), prove-it (end-of-work evidence protocol — discovers what CI actually gates, runs both static gates, checks threaded values at their terminus, performs one real persistence round-trip, and emits a claim→command→result table where anything unprovable is labeled UNVERIFIED rather than assumed), review-slop (report-only diff review with evidence, calibrated severity, validation and mock-coverage checks, and acceptance criteria), review-merge-pipeline (verify → review → fix → commit → push → PR → merge in one shot, detecting the repo's integration branch instead of assuming one), deploy (production promotion with merge strategy inferred from repository history), db-migration-safety (expand-contract sequencing, idempotent SQL, batched backfills), and backup-verify (confirms backups exist AND actually restore, via a scratch branch with smoke queries and timestamped evidence). Every skill defers to a repo-local version of itself when the project defines one.

plugins.name: work-plan
plugins.description: Track-aware daily planning over GitHub issues. Shared tracks (git-synced .work-plan/) optionally pinned to a canonical plan branch (plan-branch; push-track promotes a private track to it), AI clustering (group/auto-triage), coverage, plan-status doc liveness with drift detection, batched GraphQL fetches, and dependency-aware next-up with per-track ordering presets. Includes a theme-aware, accessible VS Code viewer — sidebar tree with a visibility×tier exposure badge, a repo-qualified Mermaid dependency graph, per-issue in-progress badge/toggle and dependency chips, next-up controls, proactive auto-slot suggestions with a compare-and-swap collision guard, and a Plans view with confirm-gated frontmatter writes and repository-contained plan links. Installer ownership is content-verified so unmanaged or modified launchers are preserved.

plugins.name: defect-scan
plugins.description: Language-aware defect hunter for Claude Code AND Codex. Detect stack -> triage by risk -> run real analyzers (ruff/mypy, tsc/eslint, rubocop/brakeman, +optional semgrep/gitleaks/bandit) -> reason with battle-tested patterns + 15 language profiles (python, react-typescript, ruby, go, csharp, java, kotlin, swift, objc, php, rust, yaml, shell, dart) -> report (confidence-tiered, severity/priority, gh-issue-correlated) -> optionally file deduped/labeled issues (--file-issues), apply safe fixes (--fix), or second-opinion via Codex (--cross-model). Runs on macOS/Linux/Windows; model-free eval harness; extensible drop-in profiles/patterns.
